keys.description: Inclusive lower bound of the day/month chunking window, parsed with DateOnly.TryParse(value, InvariantCulture) (accepts more than just the ISO form shown in the error text). Consulted only by ExportSegmentPlanner's D/M branch (ExportSegmentPlanner.cs:112); ignored when export.by is key or full. A CLI backfill window overrides it for a single run regardless of export.by: DocumentExecutor.ExecuteExportAsync rewrites the in-memory flow's FromDate (and ToDate, only if a backfill 'to' is also supplied, else the flow's own ToDate is kept) from RunParameters.BackfillFrom before invoking the runner, logging an explicit 'export window overridden by run parameters' notice; the override is a no-op on a key- or full-chunked flow since the planner never reads FromDate/ToDate there (DocumentExecutor.cs:313-321). When omitted, the runner probes the source before planning - SELECT MIN([dateColumn]), MAX([dateColumn]) under the same source.withHint and source.filter the chunk SELECTs use - and fills only the bound left open, matching what the legacy engine did before it planned its batches. The resolved window is logged as an 'export.window' event and the probe appears in trace.sql as 'source.datebounds'. Only when the source has no row with a non-NULL date does the planner fall back to its fixed window (three years before the run's start through today), which is what previously caused a history export to silently skip everything older than three years. The --from/--to run parameters set the bound for a single run, and a bound given either way is used as written rather than probed.

ExportFileWriterFactory.ResolveEncoding maps the (trimmed, uppercased) token to a .NET Encoding used by the StreamWriter that writes the header and every row. keys.description: File-name prefix for every written segment (legacy trgFileName), trimmed at load. The final per-segment name is '{prefix}{timestamp}{suffix}.{target.fileType}': timestamp is '_yyyyMMddHHmmss' or empty per target.addTimestamp, and suffix depends on export.by - a single date or a 'start-end' date range for day/month, a zero-padded 'lo-hi' key range for key, '_NullRows' for each mode's trailing NULL-value segment, or nothing at all for a full export (ExportSegmentPlanner.cs:117-165). keys.description: Destination for the exported files (legacy trgPath). Two destinations are registered and the runner selects one by CanHandle: LocalExportDestination handles a local/UNC filesystem path or a file:// URI (a location starting with 'file://' case-insensitively, or containing no '://' scheme at all), and AzureBlobExportDestination handles Azure object storage (abfss://, wasbs://, and the https://<account>.blob|dfs.core.windows.net URL forms), landing CSV/Parquet in the lake authenticated by the shared Azure credential (SQLFLOW_AZURE_AUTH) with no per-flow secret. DocumentExecutor.ExecuteExportAsync passes both into the runner (destinations: [new LocalExportDestination(), new AzureBlobExportDestination(...)], src/SqlFlow.Execution/DocumentExecutor.cs:304-307), and WithoutDatabaseExport.BuildRunner forwards a caller-supplied destinations list (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/Export/WithoutDatabaseExport.cs:22-35). A local path stays local; an abfss/wasbs/https storage path writes to the lake. Trimmed at load. A relative, non-URI value is resolved against the flow file's own directory before the run (so the sample's './out' means 'next to this YAML file', confirmed against samples/export/orders-export.flow.yaml), by DocumentLoader.ResolveRelativeExportPath, which leaves file:// URIs and Path.IsPathRooted absolute paths untouched (Execution/DocumentLoader.cs:63-75). At write time ExportFlowRunner.ComposePath trims a trailing slash or backslash and joins target.path, the segment's subfolder (from target.subfolderPattern), the composed file name, and '.' + target.fileType (ExportFlowRunner.cs:232-236).
keys.validation: "{source}: 'target.path' is required (the folder for the exported files; a local path or file:// URI)." when blank at load time (YamlExportFlowLoader.cs:208-210). Defensive run-time recheck (legacy control-database path only, unreachable via YAML): SqlFlowException "Export flow {id} has no trgPath." (ExportFlowRunner.cs:67-70). A scheme no registered destination recognizes fails every run with SqlFlowException "No export destination handles the path '<path>'." (ExportFlowRunner.cs:115-116).

keys.default: null (no subfolder; every file lands directly under target.path)
keys.appliesWhen: export.by is day or month; ExportSegmentPlanner passes an empty subfolder unconditionally for key-chunked, full, and every mode's trailing NULL-rows segment, silently ignoring this setting there
keys.description: Token pattern controlling which date levels become subfolders under target.path for a day/month-chunked segment. ExportSegmentPlanner.SubFolder upper-cases the pattern and tests it for the literal SUBSTRINGS 'YYYY', 'MM', and 'DD' (a Contains check, not a tokenizer - so an unrelated word that happens to contain one of these substrings, e.g. 'SUMMARY' containing 'MM', would also trigger that level); whichever are present each contribute one path segment, and the segments are ALWAYS emitted in the fixed order year, then month, then day, joined by '/' with a trailing '/' - the pattern only controls which levels appear, never their order (so a pattern like 'DD/MM/YYYY' still produces a '<year>/<month>/<day>/' folder, not day-first) (ExportSegmentPlanner.cs:347-372). Applied per segment using that segment's own chunk-start date.

keys.description: The single quoting character CsvExportFileWriter wraps a field in when required: by default (QuoteStringColumnsOnly = true) every string-typed reader column is quoted regardless of content, and any column (string or not) whose formatted value contains the delimiter, the qualifier itself, CR, or LF is quoted too; an embedded qualifier inside a quoted field is doubled (ExportFileWriters.cs:56-57,137-162). Only the value's single character is used (CsvWriteOptions.Qualifier is a char).

keys.description: How non-string values are rendered as CSV text. 'iso' (default) writes ISO-8601, 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.fffffff' for a DateTime. 'legacy' writes the invariant culture's own default formats, byte-for-byte as the legacy CsvHelper writer produced them (CsvConfiguration(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) called each value's ToString(IFormatProvider) with no explicit format), so a DateTime becomes 'MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm:ss' and a SQL date, read back as a midnight DateTime, 'MM/dd/yyyy 00:00:00'. Select 'legacy' when a consumer is already parsing files the old engine wrote and the port must not change what it sees; a flow mapped from a legacy flw.Export row defaults to it. The one deliberate difference in 'legacy' mode is byte[], which stays base64 rather than reproducing legacy's literal 'System.Byte[]' text that discarded the value.
keys.validation: "{source}: 'target.valueFormat' must be iso or legacy; got '<value>'." for any other token.

keys.description: Compresses each written file into a single-entry .zip in place after it is written (legacy ZipTrg), replacing the file at its location. A destination that cannot compress fails the run with 'This export destination does not support zipTrg (compression) for '<location>'.' rather than silently skipping it; both the local filesystem and the Azure Blob / ADLS Gen2 destinations implement it.
